Bing Chilling
BING CHIL-ing
phrase (Gen Alpha slang)
From a May 2021 video the wrestler and actor John Cena posted to the Chinese social network Weibo, promoting a film in Mandarin while holding an ice-cream cone: "Zaoshang hao Zhongguo, xianzai wo you bingqilin" — "Good morning, China; now I have ice cream." Bingqilin (ice cream) sounds to English ears like "bing chilling," and the clip became a global meme in 2021–22. Gen Alpha uses "bing chilling" for ice cream, for relaxing ("just bing chilling"), and as a nonsense shout.

Definition · Webster 1828 · Scriptures · Corruption · Roots · Usage · Related

Biblical Definition

"Bing chilling" is a silly way to say ice cream — or to say you’re relaxing. It comes from a video of John Cena saying "ice cream" in Chinese. The Christian observation: there is nothing to fix in a joke about ice cream, and something to enjoy. Scripture says simple pleasures are gifts: God "giveth us richly all things to enjoy" (1Ti 6:17); "Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights" (Jas 1:17). The Preacher says that to "eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it is the gift of God" (Ecc 3:13). An ice cream cone on a summer porch, a whole family laughing at a meme, a Saturday of "just chilling" — these are mercies. The only care is the ordinary one: rest is good when it follows work and leads to thanks (Exo 20:9-10), and dessert is good when it does not rule the belly (Pro 23:2). A father can tell a five-year-old: "Bing chilling! God made ice cream taste good because He loves to give us happy things. Let’s say thank You to Him before we eat it." Few slang words lead so directly to gratitude.

Webster 1828 Definition

John Cena’s Mandarin "ice cream" (bingqilin) video of May 2021 — a harmless joke for ice cream and relaxing, and a nudge toward thanks for good gifts.

expand to see more

BING CHILLING, phr. (internet meme, 2021–present; Gen Alpha usage) Ice cream; relaxing; a nonsense shout. "Just bing chilling on the couch."

From Mandarin bingqilin, ice cream, as said by John Cena (May 2021).

Decode for parents: completely harmless.

Webster 1828, the root — CHILL, n. A shivering with cold; rigors, as in an ague; the cold fit that precedes a fever; sensation of cold in an animal body; chilliness. [ See Cold and Heat .]

Key Scripture

1Ti 6:17 — "Charge them that are rich in this world, that they be not highminded, nor trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God, who giveth us richly all things to enjoy;"

Jas 1:17 — "Every good gift and every perfect gift is from above, and cometh down from the Father of lights, with whom is no variableness, neither shadow of turning."

Ecc 3:13 — "And also that every man should eat and drink, and enjoy the good of all his labour, it is the gift of God."

Pro 23:2 — "And put a knife to thy throat, if thou be a man given to appetite."

Modern Corruption

"Bing chilling" is innocent fun; its only caution is the ordinary one of rest without work and dessert without restraint.

expand to see more

There is almost nothing here to correct. The meme is cross-cultural silliness, and laughter is a gift. If anything, "just chilling" as a life motto can drift toward the sluggard’s love of ease (Pro 6:9-10), but that is a caution about habits, not the word.

Enjoy it and add thanks. A family that says grace over ice cream is teaching that every good thing comes from the Father. Let the meme be a reminder: God gives us richly all things to enjoy.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Mandarin bingqilin (ice cream) → John Cena’s Weibo video (May 2021) → global meme "bing chilling" (2021–22).

expand to see more

Mandarin bing (ice) + qilin (from English "cream") → bingqilin, ice cream

May 2021: John Cena’s Mandarin promotional video

2021–22: global meme; "bing chilling" as ice cream and relaxing

English chill — cold; slang: to relax

Usage

""Can we get bing chilling after the game?""

"God giveth us richly all things to enjoy — including bing chilling (1Ti 6:17)."

"Every good gift is from above — say thanks for the cone (Jas 1:17)."
